claims.hypothesis: HC3N around these low-mass YSOs is formed by the WCCC mechanism
claims.experiment: Compared HC3N sizes with L1527 and compared observed CH3OH/HC3N ratio with Nautilus warm-up models
claims.result: HC3N extents ~2930-3230 au similar to L1527; observed ratio in IRAS 03245 matches models at ~30-35 K
claims.finding: HC3N is formed by WCCC around IRAS 03235 and IRAS 03245

evidence.quote: We confirm that the observed ratio in IRAS 03245 agrees with the modeled values at temperatures around 30–35 K, which supports the HC$_{3}$N formation by the WCCC mechanism.

claims.hypothesis: Gas-phase CH3OH in IRAS 03245 comes from thermal desorption
claims.experiment: Compared the model temperature at matching ages with the source dust temperature and CH3OH sublimation temperature
claims.result: Matching temperatures (~31-34 K) are well below where CH3OH desorbs thermally
claims.finding: Non-thermal desorption or gas-phase formation is working for CH3OH, especially in IRAS 03245

evidence.quote: In this temperature range, CH$_{3}$OH does not thermally desorb from dust grains.
Non-thermal desorption mechanisms or gas-phase formation of CH$_{3}$OH seem to work efficiently around IRAS 03245.

claims.hypothesis: CH3OH detection depends on the envelope mass
claims.experiment: Compared CH3OH detections with envelope masses of the three sources
claims.result: Envelope masses are similar but CH3OH detected only in IRAS 03245
claims.finding: CH3OH detection is independent of envelope mass, implying chemical diversity

evidence.quote: The detection/non-detection of CH$_{3}$OH is independent of the mass of envelopes.

claims.hypothesis: HC3N distributions resemble those of carbon-chain species in the WCCC source L1527
claims.experiment: 2D Gaussian fits to HC3N moment 0 maps and size comparison with L1527
claims.result: HC3N sizes ~2930-3230 au in IRAS 03235 and IRAS 03245
claims.finding: HC3N sizes are similar to L1527 carbon-chain species

evidence.quote: Sizes of the HC$_{3}$N distributions ($\sim 2930-3230$ au) in IRAS 03235 and IRAS 03245 are similar to those of the carbon-chain species in the warm carbon chain chemistry (WCCC) source L1527.

claims.hypothesis: Higher bolometric luminosity favors non-thermal CH3OH desorption
claims.experiment: Compared Lbol of the three sources with the CH3OH detection pattern
claims.result: IRAS 03245 has the highest Lbol (4.94 Lsun) and is the only CH3OH detection
claims.finding: Luminosity seems to support the non-thermal desorption mechanisms

evidence.quote: The fact that IRAS 03245 has the highest bolometric luminosity among the target sources seems to support these mechanisms

referee_caveats_inferred: Only HC3N 16-15 (one line) constrains HC3N, so Tex and N are degenerate; the two cases differ by a factor of ~3-4 in N and the CH3OH/HC3N ratio changes from 3.7 to 16.
Resolution of ~11'' x 8'' (~3000 au) cannot separate hot-corino scales; CH3OH may be diluted so the ratio is a beam-averaged value.
CH3OH non-detections in two sources give no stated upper limits, so the ratio constraint there is qualitative.
Model ratio is compared with column-density ratio; the dependence on the path-length and source geometry is not tested.
Matching a single dust temperature per source to a model temperature depends on the dust-gas equal-temperature assumption and on one cosmic-ray/C/O grid.
